summary: ACCEPT after three rounds, with two REQUIRED follow-up tests named below. Both round-2 blockers closed and verified with a POSITIVE CONTROL on the prior blocked head: three identical calls on a bounded target give RUN3 = ZERO log records at any level on d306d8d, while HEAD still emits [OMS-CANCEL-UNCONFIRMED] carrying broker_id, last_status and reads_failed, NOT subject to the (target,path) dedup. The FRTT 2026-08-11 never-silent contract is honoured again. Field spellings aligned: one grep on outcome=refused returns 6 across both populations (2 from #829, 4 direct), target_client_order_id= likewise, and ⭐ the substring-sibling trap was checked explicitly - OMS-CANCEL-DEAD-TARGET-BOUND is NOT a substring of OMS-DIRECT-CANCEL-DEAD-TARGET-BOUND, so a naive grep -c cannot absorb one population into the other. The dedup difference is stated ON THE LINE as emission=once_per_target_path_per_process, and per_process is accurate since there is exactly one OmsRiskService per OMS process. Strand analysis executed: a live order with zero terminal refusals still reaches the broker on all four covered paths, each with an in-test one-variable pair, and fail-open holds on all six unknown inputs including a missing row and a None target id. The bound can fire only on positive durable broker evidence. 14 of 16 mutants killed. ⛔ TWO REQUIRED FOLLOW-UP TESTS, both two-liners, over behaviour HEAD already gets right. (1) A test whose NAME asserts a property it does not test: test_missing_target_row_fails_open_without_inventing_evidence exercises _record_cancel_verify_reports, NOT the gate - inverting that gate to fail CLOSED survives all 2660 tests. Under an inverted gate the verifier would treat 'no row' as 'target is dead', skip the resubmit entirely, and return having logged dead_target_bound=1 - the FRTT unowned-working-order shape returning while wearing a label that says the opposite. Assert _verify_cancel_landed with a random target_order_id still submits a resubmit. (2) The bounded-drift-abandons-its-intent property is NOT pinned: the existing assertion holds because the intent is abandoned on the first UNBOUNDED pass. On a candidate bounded on its FIRST drift pass the mutant leaves intent.status='submitted' - a permanently stuck intent that occupies the #644 entry-composition cap and suppresses new entries for that symbol with ZERO broker traffic to reveal it. Seed the terminal event before the first _run_drift_cancel. ⛔ CORRECTION TO MY OWN ROUND-2 CREDIT: I recorded that the client_order_id-key mutant dies. It dies only against an ORM-identity-map mutant; a DB-level coid mutant survives, because the collision test assigns the duplicate coid in memory under no_autoflush while the DB still holds the original. That is NOT a defect - BrokerOrder.client_order_id is unique=True so coid maps 1:1 to BrokerOrder.id in production, making it an equivalent mutant - but the credit was narrower than I stated and a future reviewer should not over-trust it. MINOR: the cancel_exit_pair (Webull) exclusion is declared only in the test-module docstring, not beside the call site at service.py:2566. The dedup set is still never pruned - a handful of entries per day, not a live risk. And [OMS-CANCEL-UNCONFIRMED] now carries two opposite meanings discriminated by dead_target_bound=0|1 while the prose is written for the first; the field is on the line so a watch can split it, and no ops/ watch parses either marker today.
